name: Holy Rollers
label: Dischord
lede: Holy Rollers were a DC trio who, in 1989, did what nobody else in the Dischord orbit was doing: all three sang at once, in harmony.

eras.title: Three voices, one church basement
eras.text: DC hardcore ran on one singer and a lot of shouting. Holy Rollers split the mic three ways, drew on no wave, LA hardcore and first-wave punk, and played their first show on a bill with Fugazi, the band everyone in town was watching.

years.h: Holy Rollers start as a trio where everybody sings
years.p: Marc Lambiotte plays guitar, Joe Aronstamn bass and Maria Jones drums, and all three sing. Dischord says they may not have been the first DC punk band with every member on vocals, but certainly the first to sing three-part harmonies.
years.xp: Wikipedia says the name came from Malcolm X's autobiography, and calls them the first DC punk band to work in three-part harmony.

years.h: The first gig is an opening slot for Fugazi
years.p: Holy Rollers debut at the Wilson Center, a hall in the basement of a former church in Mount Pleasant, on a March 24 bill with [[Fugazi|233fc3f3-6de2-465c-985e-e721dbabbace]], [[Swiz|eea2f3d8-1e94-436c-ae66-4633f99f55be]] and Edsel, per Wikipedia.
years.xp:
The Wilson Center was the default all-ages room for that stretch of DC punk, a church basement where Positive Force benefits and Dischord bands took turns. Dischord's own history of the band starts right there: Holy Rollers going on first, Fugazi, barely a year old, headlining.

Wikipedia says Holy Rollers went on to play with Jawbox and Shudder to Think later in 1989.

years.h: Their first record is an EP called The Origami Sessions
years.p: Wikipedia credits it to Dischord and Adult Swim Records. It isn't in Dischord's own catalog listing for the band.

eras.title: Harmonies in a hardcore town
eras.text: Dischord calls Holy Rollers one of the more active bands in an underground getting more political by the year. They put out two albums in two years, wrote about street life and being broke in DC, and kept the studio door open for friends.

yt: "Eleventy" and "What You Said" live at the 9:30 Club, March 3, 1990
years.h: As Is is Dischord No. 42, and it doesn't stay in one genre
years.p: Trouser Press on Holy Rollers' debut album: the band's enthusiasm for punk-rock variety, running from no wave to straightforward punk to acoustic country balladeering.
years.xp: Trouser Press found the album harder to describe by individual tracks than by that appetite. Its verdict: the band had "a remarkable range of musical knowledge that adequately supplements their limited musical abilities."

years.cap: Holy Rollers' drummer behind the kit, UConn, 1991
q: Fugazi filtered through the Soft Boys.
years.p: Dischord No. 58 has ten songs, from Changeling to the title track, still the classic trio. [[Ian MacKaye|c12f644b-1066-4ead-b0dd-d0c380f5cca2]] guests on "Perfect Sleeper", one of two songs Trouser Press hears as being about money trouble in DC.
years.xp:
Trouser Press found Fabuley more diverse than the debut and thought the band's rough edges came off "more charming than deadly." The magazine counts "Perfect Sleeper" and "Cross the Line" as songs about the precarious finances of people living in the District, or on its streets.

Dischord paired it with the debut on a single CD, Fabuley + As Is (No. 59), which is how most people outside DC first heard them. The band also recorded and played with spoken-word artist Juliana Luecking, and Dischord's bio says friends wandered into the studio often.

years.h: Holy Rollers and Cringer share a 7" on Shred of Dignity
years.p: Wikipedia lists the split single on Shred of Dignity Records, a one-off step away from Dischord.

eras.title: Richmond reinforcements
eras.text: Losing a drummer usually ends a trio. Holy Rollers took on two players from Richmond, Virginia, turned into a four-piece with a second guitar, and kept going until 1995.

years.h: Jones heads to San Francisco; [[Ed Trask|0cf5525b-a45c-4e1d-b269-d306b793d442]] takes the drums
years.p: Dischord says Jones left for San Francisco and was replaced by Trask, a friend from Richmond, Virginia, who is known there now as a painter of big public murals. Wikipedia says Jones joined queercore band [[Tribe 8|10df0f02-bd7c-4193-91aa-dc3222e0f37d]].

years.cap: Flyer for Holy Rollers, Helium, Dirt and Greyhouse, Old Cambridge Baptist Church, Cambridge MA, Feb. 12, 1993
years.h: [[Chris Maynard Bopst|e258b83f-947f-466a-a75b-9d26fda2f1e3]] takes the bass and the band becomes a four-piece
years.p: Dischord says the band asked Chris Bopst to play bass and Aronstamn moved to second guitar. With Trask on drums, the rhythm section is all Richmond.
It lands ahead of the band's self-titled third album.

years.h: The third album is recorded at Inner Ear with John Morand
years.p: Holy Rollers, Dischord No. 86, is the first LP from the four-piece. Trouser Press thought the new line-up narrowed its vision toward tried-and-true DC rock.
years.xp:
Trouser Press: "The new lineup's Holy Rollers suffers from the changes," the band "cutting back on the vocal intricacy and the thematic diversity."

A full show from Gent, Belgium, on October 3, 1993, shows the four-piece live.

years.h: Six years in, Holy Rollers call it quits
years.p: Dischord's listing gives the active run as winter 1989 to 1995.

eras.title: Positive Force calls them back
eras.text: Thirty years on, the benefit-show collective that shaped their scene turned 40 and asked old bands to play. Holy Rollers said yes, then kept going.

years.h: Thirty years later, Holy Rollers play for Positive Force
years.p: Lambiotte, Aronstamn and Trask play the activist group's 40th anniversary, a five-day run of shows and protests that also brought back [[Swiz|eea2f3d8-1e94-436c-ae66-4633f99f55be]], who shared their first bill.
years.xp:
WTOP's preview puts Holy Rollers on the June 21 benefit at St. Stephen's Church for the Gaza Soup Kitchen and We Are Family D.C., with Soulside and Tsunami. Swiz played the night before.

The Black Cat's bio says the reunion became an ongoing project instead of a one-off.

yt: Full set, Union Pool, Brooklyn, July 30, 2026
years.h: The Black Cat headline, with Graham McCulloch on bass
years.p: [[Graham McCulloch|a9cb94ec-b297-44d5-9ea1-dbefe4b26c33]] joins on bass in 2026, and Holy Rollers headline D.C.'s Black Cat with [[Hammered Hulls|64368968-d520-49ea-a248-9ccc29e1467f]] and The Owners.
years.xp: Doors at 7:30 p.m. Five days later the band played Union Pool in Brooklyn; a full recording of that set is online. Wikipedia lists McCulloch as formerly of Negative Approach.
